days.title: Landing in Rome
days.kicker: ROME — Hotel Trame, by the Pantheon
days.note: Jet-lag day. Nothing ticketed, nothing timed — the only fixed point is dinner.

items.title: Land at FCO
items.detail: Immigration + bags, about 45 min

items.title: Private driver to Hotel Trame
items.detail: Pre-booked NCC, meeting you inside arrivals with a name board. Licensed cars may enter the ZTL to set down, so you are dropped at the hotel door — no garage, no walk with the bags.

items.title: Check in at Hotel Trame
items.detail: A former Franciscan monastery a few streets off Campo de' Fiori

items.title: First walk: Pantheon → Piazza Navona → Campo de' Fiori
items.detail: The Pantheon is an eight-minute walk. Go before the nap, not after.

items.title: Nap, deliberately
items.detail: Set an alarm. This is the single best defence against day-two jet lag.

items.title: Aperitivo at Etabli
items.detail: Or the Campari bar on Campo de' Fiori

items.title: Dinner — Armando al Pantheon
items.detail: Tiny, family-run, and booked out weeks ahead. Reserve now.

days.title: The Vatican, before anyone else
days.note: Early entry is the whole point: the Sistine Chapel is a different room with 40 people in it than with 400.

items.title: Vatican early-entry private tour
items.detail: Into the Sistine Chapel before general admission

items.title: Lunch — Da Romolo or Hostaria Dino e Tony
items.detail: Unfussy Roman cooking a short walk from the museum exit

items.title: Back to the hotel through the heat
items.detail: Late August in Rome peaks around 3pm. Don't fight it.

items.title: Castel Sant'Angelo, then the bridge at sunset
items.detail: Ponte Sant'Angelo with Bernini's angels catching the last light

items.title: Rooftop aperitivo near Campo de' Fiori
OPERA — arias at All Saints' Anglican Church
items.detail: Confirm the Aug 25 programme; Via del Babuino, off Piazza di Spagna

items.title: Late dinner — Pierluigi
items.detail: Seafood on Piazza de' Ricci; a properly Roman hour to eat

days.title: Ancient Rome, end to end
days.note: Last Roman day before the north — this afternoon is also the Villa Borghese photo session, so the siesta runs shorter than usual.
days.changeNote: The old evening Galleria Borghese slot was already near dark and needed a timed museum ticket. Swapped for actual daylight in the gardens, no ticket required — Trastevere moves later to take the evening instead.

items.title: Colosseum with arena floor, then Forum + Palatine
items.detail: The arena-floor add-on is worth it — you stand where the sand was

items.title: Lunch — Roscioli
items.detail: Carbonara and cacio e pepe, and the deli counter on the way out
items.how: Walk, 5 min via Campo de' Fiori

items.title: Siesta
items.detail: Shorter than the other days — the light at Borghese is worth trading a bit of rest for

items.title: Villa Borghese Gardens, in the daylight
items.detail: Rome's largest park — shaded avenues, the Fontana dei Cavalli Marini, and the Pincio terrace over Piazza del Popolo with St. Peter's dome on the skyline. Soft light under the trees most of the afternoon — good ground for pictures. The Galleria itself needs a timed ticket booked weeks out; skip it unless you already have one.

items.title: Down to Piazza del Popolo
items.detail: The twin churches and the obelisk, down the Pincio steps

items.title: Trastevere on foot
items.detail: Cross the Tiber and wander to Piazza Santa Maria in Trastevere

items.title: Dinner — Da Enzo al 29
items.detail: Trastevere, twelve tables, no reservations after 9pm

days.title: North to Florence by Frecciarossa
days.changeNote: Now high-speed rail rather than a self-drive up the A1. Orvieto came off with the car — the Frecciarossa does not stop there, and reaching it by regional train would cost the whole day.

items.title: Check out; taxi to Roma Termini
items.detail: About fifteen minutes from Campo de' Fiori. Aim to be at the platform twenty minutes before departure.

items.title: Frecciarossa — Roma Termini → Firenze S.M.N.
items.detail: Book Trenitalia or Italo well ahead; advance fares are a fraction of the walk-up price and both run the route hourly.

items.title: Arrive Firenze Santa Maria Novella
items.detail: The station is a nine-minute walk from Via dei Rondinelli — no transfer needed

items.title: Drop bags at Casa G. Firenze
items.detail: Via dei Rondinelli, between the Duomo and Santa Maria Novella. Rooms are ready from 3:00pm; they will hold luggage until then.

items.title: Lunch at the Mercato Centrale
items.detail: Five minutes north — the upstairs food hall, no booking, no ceremony

items.title: First orientation walk
items.detail: The Duomo and Baptistery from the outside, then Piazza della Repubblica and down to the Arno. The ticketed interiors are all tomorrow — today is just getting your bearings.

items.title: Unpack and reset
items.detail: The train bought you an afternoon the drive would have eaten

items.title: Aperitivo on the secret patio
items.detail: Casa G.'s courtyard bar

items.title: OPERA — La Traviata at St. Mark's Anglican
items.detail: Via Maggio, across Ponte Santa Trinita — booked for arrival evening, comfortably clear now the train lands you at midday.

items.title: Dinner — Trattoria Sostanza
items.detail: Cash only. The butter chicken and the tortino. Alternative: Buca dell'Orafo.

days.title: All of Florence in one day
days.changeNote: Absorbs the Accademia and the Duomo climb from the old arrival day. Three timed entries before lunch — book all three now, in this order.
days.note: Dense by design. Everything before 1pm is ticketed and time-stamped; everything after is yours.

items.title: Accademia — David at first entry
items.detail: Forty-five minutes is genuinely enough. Go straight down the hall.

items.title: Duomo — climb Brunelleschi's dome
items.detail: 463 steps, timed slot, and much better before the day heats up

items.title: Coffee on Piazza della Signoria
items.detail: The Loggia dei Lanzi is an open-air sculpture hall and it is free

items.title: Uffizi, guided
items.detail: Botticelli, Leonardo, the Caravaggio room. Roughly two hours with a guide.

items.title: Lunch in the Oltrarno — Il Santo Bevitore
items.detail: Or Gucci Osteria if you want the splurge. Trattoria Mario is the third option if you'd rather eat near San Lorenzo.

items.title: Pitti Palace and the Boboli Gardens
items.detail: The gardens are the reason to go; climb to the top for the view back over the city

items.title: Oltrarno artisan workshops
items.detail: Via Maggio and Santo Spirito — gilders, leatherworkers, restorers still working street level

items.title: Ponte Vecchio, then up to Piazzale Michelangelo
items.detail: Sunset is around 8:00pm. Taxi up, walk down.

items.title: Dinner — Borgo San Jacopo
items.detail: Michelin-starred, on the river, with a handful of window tables. Ask for one.

days.title: Into the Val d'Elsa, through Certaldo

items.title: Check out; collect the rental car
items.detail: The agencies cluster on Borgo Ognissanti, ~10 min on foot and just outside the ZTL — so you never drive into the centro storico. Have the IDP and licence ready.

items.title: Southwest out of the city
items.detail: Florence → Certaldo is about 45 minutes

items.title: Certaldo Alto, by funicular
items.detail: Boccaccio's birthplace — a walled brick town, the funicular climbs from Piazza Boccaccio in under two minutes

items.title: Casa Boccaccio
items.detail: The Decameron's author was born here; the house is now a small, quiet museum

items.title: Lunch on Via Boccaccio
items.detail: A terrace table in the upper town before the drive on

items.title: On to Castelfalfi
items.detail: About twenty-five minutes further into the Val d'Elsa

items.title: Check in — Il Castelfalfi
items.detail: A restored 14th-century hamlet on a 2,700-acre estate, its own castle at the centre

items.title: The hamlet on foot
items.detail: The piazza, the castle walls, the little church — all restored, none of it roped off

items.title: Aperitivo at Ecrù
items.detail: The estate's cocktail bar

items.title: Dinner — La Via del Sale
items.detail: The estate's fine-dining room; the vegetables and olive oil are grown on the property

items.title: Driver to San Gimignano
items.detail: About twenty-five minutes

items.title: The towers of San Gimignano
items.detail: Fourteen of the original seventy-two medieval towers still stand — best seen from Piazza della Cisterna

items.title: The Collegiata
items.detail: Ghirlandaio and Gozzoli frescoes wall to wall in a church the size of a chapel

items.title: Gelato at Dondoli
items.detail: A two-time world gelato champion, right on Piazza della Cisterna

items.title: Lunch + a Vernaccia tasting
items.detail: San Gimignano's own DOCG white, crisp and mineral, made for a hot afternoon

items.title: Driver to Volterra
items.detail: About forty-five minutes

items.title: Piazza dei Priori and the Roman theatre
items.detail: Tuscany's most complete medieval civic square, plus a 1st-century BC theatre still being excavated

items.title: Alabaster workshops
items.detail: A carving tradition here since Etruscan times — several studios welcome walk-ins

items.title: Drive back to Castelfalfi
items.detail: About fifty minutes

items.title: Dinner at the resort
items.detail: Or a quieter table down in Montaione village

days.title: Chianti, then the estate
days.note: A slower day by design after two touring days — golf or the spa in the morning, wine after lunch.

items.title: The estate's 27-hole course, or the spa
items.detail: Tuscany's largest golf course, or a morning at the newly renovated spa

items.title: Driver to Montespertoli
items.detail: About forty minutes

items.title: A Chianti Montespertoli estate
items.detail: The smallest Chianti DOCG sub-zone, carved out of the old Colli Fiorentini in 1997 — quieter than Chianti Classico proper

items.title: The village and a second cellar
items.detail: Small enough to see on foot between tastings

items.title: Back to Castelfalfi
items.detail: About forty minutes

items.title: The pool or the spa terrace at sunset
Dinner — Giglio Blu or La Via del Sale
items.detail: Something casual, or a second night at the estate's fine-dining room

days.title: South by rail, Castelfalfi to Naples
days.kicker: TUSCANY → NAPLES — return the car in Florence, then the train
days.changeNote: Was a straight five-hour self-drive to Naples. The confirmed Florence → Naples train only departs from Firenze S.M.N., so the car goes back first — the rental ends here, not on Sep 6.
days.note: Reservation #21586310US4 ends today, in Florence — fill the tank before you get there.

items.title: Check out; drive to Florence
items.detail: Back the way you came — about ninety minutes, less traffic than the Friday-afternoon drive in

items.title: Drop off the rental car
items.detail: Borgo Ognissanti, near Firenze S.M.N. — reservation #21586310US4 ends here

items.title: Coffee, then the platform
items.detail: A buffer before the train — Frecciarossa 9413 doesn't wait

items.title: Frecciarossa 9413 to Naples
items.detail: Firenze S.M.N. → Napoli Centrale, direct — 3h15. Super Economy fare, from €71.80.

items.title: Check in — De Bonart, Curio Collection
items.detail: An art palazzo on Via Partenope in Chiaia, facing the bay

items.title: Rooftop aperitivo
items.detail: Vesuvius on one side, the bay on the other

items.title: Dinner — pizza at Sorbillo
items.detail: Via dei Tribunali. You are in the city that invented it; do this before anything fancier.

days.title: Capri, by ferry
days.note: Weather-dependent. The Blue Grotto only opens in a flat sea — treat it as a bonus, not a plan. Buy the return leg when you buy the outbound, and check the last sailing before you settle in for the afternoon.

items.title: Walk down to Molo Beverello
items.detail: The fast-ferry pier is fifteen minutes along the seafront from the hotel

items.title: Fast ferry — Naples → Capri
items.detail: NLG, SNAV and Caremar all run it in about fifty minutes. Sailings are frequent in September but sell out at the counter — book online the night before.

items.title: The Faraglioni, the grottoes, the swim coves
items.detail: Pick up a round-the-island boat at Marina Grande — Blue Grotto if the sea is calm enough to enter

items.title: Lunch — Da Paolino
items.detail: Under the lemon trees. Il Riccio is the Michelin alternative, on the cliff by the grotto.

items.title: The Piazzetta and the Gardens of Augustus
items.detail: Gelato on the terrace above Via Krupp

items.title: Ferry back to Naples
items.detail: Check the final sailing when you arrive — the last fast boats go early evening, and missing one means a night on the island

items.title: Dinner — Palazzo Petrucci
items.detail: Michelin-starred Neapolitan tasting menu, back in the old city — the celebration dinner for the boat day

days.title: Naples, then the coast
days.changeNote: Pompeii is dropped — there's no rental car to route through it with. This is a private driver straight down the coast road instead.
days.note: No rental car this leg — book a private driver for the coast road.

items.title: Pizza for breakfast — Di Matteo
items.detail: Also on Via dei Tribunali, a few doors from last night's Sorbillo. Yes, at 8:30am. It's Naples.

items.title: Spaccanapoli
items.detail: The dead-straight Greek road that still splits the old city in half

items.title: Check out; last look at the bay
Private driver to Amalfi
items.detail: Coast road via Vietri — narrow, slow, spectacular. Sit back, someone else is driving.

items.title: Check in — Anantara Convento di Amalfi
items.detail: A 13th-century monastery on the cliff edge, with the original cloister still standing

items.title: The beach club, by cliff lift
items.detail: A slow afternoon at sea level after the drive

items.title: Dinner — Dei Cappuccini
items.detail: The hotel's Michelin room, or La Locanda for pizza if the day has beaten you

days.title: Ravello, above everything
days.note: The Ravello Festival runs to Sep 5. Check tonight's programme — the stage is built out over the cliff at Villa Rufolo. The switchbacks up from the coast are tight and slow even with a car; with no rental this leg at all, have the hotel call a local driver.

items.title: A slow morning on the cloister terrace
items.detail: The one unhurried morning on the coast — use it

items.title: Lunch — Lo Scoglio
items.detail: Nerano. The original spaghetti alla Nerano, and worth the boat ride on its own.

items.title: Up to Ravello
items.detail: Forty-five minutes of switchbacks above the coast

items.title: Villa Cimbrone
items.detail: The Terrace of Infinity — a marble balustrade lined with busts, and a thousand-foot drop to the sea

items.title: RAVELLO FESTIVAL — check the Sep 4 programme
items.detail: Confirmed concerts run to Sep 5, so both your Amalfi nights are inside the festival window.

items.title: Late dinner — Il Flauto di Pan
items.detail: In the Villa Cimbrone gardens. Rossellinis is the other option.

days.title: Back to Rome, by rail
days.kicker: AMALFI → NAPLES → ROME — driver, then train
days.changeNote: Was a straight four-hour self-drive. There's no rental car by this point — a private driver back to Naples, then the train, covers the same ground.

items.title: Check out; last look at the coast
items.detail: Breakfast on the cloister terrace before you give the room back

items.title: Private driver to Naples
items.detail: Back along the coast road to Napoli Centrale

items.title: Arrive Napoli Centrale; drop bags, coffee
Frecciarossa to Rome
items.detail: Napoli Centrale → Roma Termini, direct — about 1h10. Frequent departures; no need to book far ahead.

items.title: Arrive Roma Termini; taxi to the hotel
Check in — The St. Regis Rome
items.detail: The hotel is inside Rome's ZTL — use valet or a garage nearby; don't try to park at the curb.

items.title: Last Roman afternoon
items.detail: Piazza di Spagna and the windows along Via Condotti

items.title: Aperitivo at Lumen
items.detail: The St. Regis bar — the grand-hotel version of a last night

items.title: Farewell dinner — Aroma
items.detail: A rooftop table level with the top tier of the Colosseum. Imago is the alternative, over the Spanish Steps.

items.title: Taxi to FCO
items.detail: About forty minutes on an empty Sunday road. No rental to return this time — that ended in Florence on Sep 1.

items.title: Check in and bag drop
items.detail: Three hours ahead for an intercontinental departure

items.title: FCO → IAH
items.detail: Arrivederci, Italia.

driversNote: You are car-free for the first five days: a private driver in from FCO, taxis and your feet in Rome, the Frecciarossa to Florence. The rental is only collected on Aug 29, on Borgo Ognissanti just outside Florence's ZTL, and returned in Florence again on Sep 1 before the Naples train — three driving days, not fourteen. Everything south of that (Naples, Capri, Amalfi, and the ride back to Rome) is ferry, private driver or train, never a car you're driving yourself. The IDP ships by Aug 3; pack it with the physical licence, not just a photo of it. Never drive into either historic centre — Florence's ZTL alone is ~€200 a crossing. Castelfalfi has its own parking. Budget roughly €40 in tolls for the Florence–Tuscany stretch and a full tank each way.

bookings.item: Book Casa G. Firenze for Aug 27–29
bookings.detail: Two nights in Florence, wedged between Rome and Tuscany — the tightest hotel window on the trip.

bookings.item: Reserve dinners at Il Castelfalfi — La Via del Sale, Aug 29 & 31
bookings.detail: The estate's fine-dining room. Worth booking ahead even though the room itself is already confirmed.

bookings.item: Rebook the rental car — Florence pickup and drop-off, not FCO
bookings.detail: Reservation #21586310US4 is still FCO Aug 24 → FCO Sep 6. It needs to become Borgo Ognissanti, Florence, Aug 29 → Florence Sep 1: three days rather than fourteen, both ends in the same city. A different pickup/drop-off city usually carries a fee, so the €1,087.81 quote will not hold — re-quote before cancelling.

bookings.item: Book the FCO → Hotel Trame private driver
bookings.detail: Pre-booked NCC, meeting you inside arrivals with a name board — roughly €70–90 for the two of you, against a €55 flat-rate official taxi if you would rather just walk to the rank. Give them the ITA flight number so the driver tracks the landing.

bookings.item: Frecciarossa tickets — Roma Termini → Firenze S.M.N., Aug 27
bookings.detail: Trenitalia and Italo both run the route hourly in about 1h30. Advance fares open around four months out and are a fraction of the walk-up price, so book as soon as the date is loaded. Aim for a departure around 10:35am.

bookings.item: Florence opera — La Traviata at St. Mark's, Aug 27
bookings.detail: The train lands you at midday, so the evening is no longer tight — but book it before the seats go.

bookings.item: Rome opera — All Saints' Anglican, Aug 25
bookings.detail: Confirm the programme is posted before booking.

bookings.item: Montespertoli estate visit for Mon Aug 31
bookings.detail: A Chianti Montespertoli producer, plus lunch — most require an appointment rather than taking walk-ins.

bookings.item: Timed entries — Accademia, Duomo dome, Uffizi, all on Aug 28
bookings.detail: Three in one morning, in that order. Book the dome climb first; it has the fewest slots.

bookings.item: Vatican early entry (Aug 25), Colosseum arena floor (Aug 26)
bookings.detail: Both need booking — the Vatican slots go first. Pompeii is dropped from the itinerary, so there's no third guide to book here.

bookings.item: Arrange private drivers — Naples → Amalfi (Sep 3) and Amalfi → Naples (Sep 5)
bookings.detail: No rental car for either leg. Book a local car service for the coast road in both directions — the hotel can usually arrange this directly.

bookings.item: Capri ferry — Naples → Capri return, Sep 2
bookings.detail: Fast ferries from Molo Beverello take about fifty minutes; NLG, SNAV and Caremar all run the route. Book both legs online the night before rather than queueing at the counter, and note the last sailing back. The round-the-island boat can be picked up at Marina Grande on the day.

bookings.item: Ravello Festival — check the Sep 4 programme
bookings.detail: Festival runs to Sep 5, so both Amalfi nights now fall inside the window. The Aug 29 Mahler date still lands on your Florence→Castelfalfi transfer, so it was never reachable.
Frecciarossa runs the route roughly every half hour, about 1h10 — no need to lock this in until closer to the date.
Sostanza Aug 27 · Borgo San Jacopo Aug 28 · La Via del Sale Aug 29 & 31 · San Gimignano lunch Aug 30. Plus Armando, Roscioli, Lo Scoglio — reserve ahead where they take bookings.

bookingsRuledOut.reason: Needs a Verona overnight, and Sep 4 is your Ravello night on the Amalfi Coast.

budget.note: 6 hotels, 13 nights. Trame ($1,571.58), Castelfalfi ($3,764.98) and De Bonart ($1,071, confirmed) are actual bookings; Convento is a quote, 2 nights rather than 3. The St. Regis is still an estimate.

Holding the old total pending a re-quote: the rental drops from 14 days to 3 (Florence Aug 29 → Florence Sep 1, both ends the same city now), but a one-way-turned-round-trip re-quote could move that either way. New costs: the FCO private transfer (~€70–90), two Frecciarossa fares, and private drivers for both Naples↔Amalfi legs. Rome and FCO parking are gone entirely.

Vatican, Colosseum, Capri, wineries, Florence galleries, operas. Held pending a re-quote: swapping the private Lucibello charter for the Capri ferry takes a four-figure line down to about €50 of tickets for the two of you, and dropping Pompeii removes a guide fee, so this should come down materially.
Taxis, tips, Naples street food, incidentals.

photographers.spots: Pincio terrace and Villa Borghese at sunset; the Colosseum and Trevi at dawn, empty; the Spanish Steps
Piazzale Michelangelo at sunset; Ponte Vecchio at dawn; the Uffizi loggia
San Gimignano's towers at golden hour; the Castelfalfi vineyards and golf course; Volterra's alabaster studios
Positano's pastel stairs and Spiaggia Grande; Amalfi Drive viewpoints; the Ravello gardens
Gardens of Augustus over the Faraglioni; Via Krupp; Marina Grande
